title: No recoverable collective intent; distinguishing must state material facts
subject: realist-standing-rules
ratio:
No mechanism in this registry may presuppose recoverable collective intent: the "will" of a
multi-agent council or session is not a discoverable fact, and appeals to it are normative moves
dressed as descriptions, not descriptions -- mechanisms record DECLARED reasoning only, never
inferred intent. "Following precedent" is never mechanical, because material facts can always be
re-described: internal and external distinguishing operate literally by changing the description
of the facts a ratio is applied to. Anti-evasion design must therefore constrain fact
re-description itself, not merely rule citation: every distinguishing move must state (a) WHICH
material facts differ from the target record's facts and (b) WHY the difference is material to
the ratio's application -- an unstated or immaterial distinction is not a legitimate distinguishing
act. Legal/institutional certainty is not a property a text has by itself; it is an achievement
produced by disciplined, auditable interpretive process -- which is this registry's own value
proposition, and the reason every record here is a disposition (text) whose norm (meaning) is
produced, contestably, by reading it, and every precedent is itself a second-degree document: the
recorded product of a prior interpretation of other materials, open in turn to reinterpretation.
scope_conditions: any mechanism design proposal for this layer
any distinguishing record's statement of differing facts
revisit_trigger: Revisit if a mechanism presupposing recoverable collective intent is ever proposed for this layer
validity_conditions: PRECEDENT.md v1 carries the fact-re-description constraint and the second-degree-documents frame
